name: Tennessee
headline_status: Marijuana is illegal; only low-THC cannabis oil is allowed for qualifying patients.
summary: Tennessee has no medical marijuana program and has not legalized or decriminalized cannabis. Possessing half an ounce or less is a misdemeanor that can bring up to a year in jail. Patients with a qualifying condition may possess CBD oil with no more than 0.9% THC, but they must buy it outside the state. Under a 2025 law, the Alcoholic Beverage Commission took over hemp-derived THC products on January 1, 2026, sales are limited to adults 21 and over, and THCA products became illegal to sell after June 30, 2026.

medical_program.value: No medical marijuana program. Patients with a qualifying condition and proper documentation may possess CBD oil containing no more than 0.9% THC. There is no in-state source, so it has to be bought in another state.

penalties.value: Possessing half an ounce or less is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year in jail. Since 2016, a third offense is no longer a felony.

hemp_thc.value: Under Public Chapter 526 (HB 1376, 2025), products may not exceed 0.3% total THC, counting THCA. Products with any THCp are banned, and sales are limited to adults 21+.

regulator.value: No cannabis regulator. Since January 1, 2026, the Tennessee Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) licenses hemp-derived cannabinoid suppliers, wholesalers and retailers. The Department of Agriculture still regulates hemp farming.

purchase_age.value: 21 or older for hemp-derived cannabinoid products; retail premises must also restrict entry to adults 21+.

retail_sales.value: Marijuana sales are illegal. Hemp-derived products may be sold only at 21+ venues such as package stores and bars; grocery, convenience and gas-station sales are excluded, and online sales and delivery are prohibited.

timeline.event: The first CBD oil law (SB 2531) is enacted.
HB 1478 takes effect, ending felony treatment for a third possession conviction.
SB 118 lets qualifying patients possess CBD oil with up to 0.9% THC and expands the list of conditions.
HB 1376 (Public Chapter 526) is enacted, moving hemp-derived cannabinoid regulation to the TABC.
The TABC takes over licensing of hemp-derived cannabinoid products.
HB1972/SB1603 bars the state from rescheduling cannabis until lawmakers create a regulatory framework.
Legacy hemp licenses lapse, effectively ending retail sales of high-THCA products.

faq.a: No. Tennessee has no recreational or medical marijuana law, and possessing even half an ounce can bring up to a year in jail.
Not for sale anymore. The 2025 hemp law counts THCA toward the 0.3% THC cap, and the window for selling existing THCA stock under older licenses closed on June 30, 2026.

faq.q: Can patients use CBD oil in Tennessee?
faq.a: Yes, if they have a qualifying condition and the right documentation. The oil may contain no more than 0.9% THC, and it has to be bought outside Tennessee.

faq.q: How old do you have to be to buy hemp THC products in Tennessee?
faq.a: 21. Since 2026, stores selling these products must also keep anyone under 21 off the premises.
